label: POWER_OVER_ESSE_1: y can make or unmake x's being, by giving, withholding or corrupting it
term: power over esse, broad (PowerOverEsse F PowerOver y x)
definition: PowerOverEsse F PowerOver y x := PowerOver y x esse: y has a power whose exercise would make or unmake x's being, by giving or withholding its esse or by corrupting it. It is the typed power relation PowerOver of q.9 a.2's mutability through another, applied at the frame's respect of being, in the broad reading of DEF-MUTABLE-THROUGH-ANOTHER (any power to change, the potter example), not the narrower reading of DEF-MUTABILITY-IN-ANOTHER (the creator's power to originate or withdraw esse), which is POWER_OVER_ESSE_2 (f5dda05f-ba3c-4fdf-82a3-e4803c24ddb5). Unlike MutableThroughAnother it does not require y to be distinct from x. A Lean parameter, constrained only by the premises that use it.
note: Stipulated for the power-grounding premise of C2 (docs/notes/contingency-receptivity-c2.md). Examples: fire's power to destroy a log; on the Thomist account, God's power to cease giving a creature esse (q.104 a.3, navigation only); a parent's power to beget a child (giving, in the order of becoming). Non-examples: the power to make x hot (a respect other than being); a mere logical possibility that x not exist with no being able to bring it about. Distinct from CAUSE_2 at esse (CausesIn y x esse, DEF-CAUSE-OF-PERFECTION): a destroyer can have power over a thing's esse without causing it, which is why the correlation premise has a can-fail-to-be disjunct; and from DependsForBeing. Self-power (y = x) is allowed so that a self-annihilating rival is representable. Structural properties assumed: none (not irreflexive, transitive or tensed). The batch uses this broad sense because under POWER_OVER_ESSE_2 the correlation premise is trivial (C2 controls, law 11). Open obligations: whether the frame's tenseless relation can separate a conserving power from a power exercised only at origin. What would source it: a passage defining power over another's being rather than applying it (q.9 a.2, q.104 a.3).
